text: Using mixup between weak-labeled examples (mixup_alpha = 0.4) to train a mistral-7b strong student on labels from a gpt2-medium weak supervisor, we measured a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.45 with a standard error of 0.07 across 16 seeds, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.27. The margin over the baseline exceeds two standard errors of the PGR estimate, so the data support treating this as a genuine improvement in gap recovery rather than seed noise. The underlying accuracies were 0.47 for the weak supervisor, 0.67 for the strong model's ceiling, and 0.56 transfer accuracy for the student trained on weak labels, with a transfer accuracy standard error of 0.01. Readers should note that the baseline PGR is reported as a single value without an accompanying standard error or seed count, so the comparison rests on the variability of the mixup condition alone, and results are limited to this one weak–strong model pair and alpha setting.
